title: Card set metadata (set.json)
description: Identity, contents, and provenance of one card set. Rows live in the CSV files this document declares; see schema/1.0/ROW-FORMAT.md.

schema_version.description: Version of this standard the document conforms to.

id.description: Permanent UUIDv4, assigned once, never changed. Survives renames and moves; consumers key on this, never on name or path.

name.description: Display name as the product is known, e.g. "2025 Topps Series 1".

slug.description: Kebab-case directory name of this set. Must match the containing directory.

sport.description: Vocabulary grows by amending this schema, never by free text.

manufacturer.description: As branded on the product, e.g. "Topps".

checklists.description: Every CSV file in this set's directory must be declared here, and vice versa. Card numbers are unique within a file, not across files: short-print variations legitimately reuse base card numbers.

then.description: A variation is always a variation of something.

file.description: Path relative to this set's directory. The folder matches `kind`. Parallel row files live under parallels/ and are declared by `parallels[].file`, never here — a parallel is not a checklist of its own.

name.description: Subset name as printed, title-cased, e.g. "Base", "Generation Now".

kind.description: base — the cards that define the set's numbering. variation — often called an image variation, short print (SP) or super short print (SSP); features a completely different photo or design element from the standard base card, while retaining the same base set card number. insert, autograph, relic — cards issued alongside the set; they have their own numbering unless they declare `varies`. Parallels are never a kind: every parallel lives in `parallels[]`. A checklist carries only card number, name and team, so it can never prove whether the photograph changed: kind follows what the manufacturer prints, and is corrected by a person with evidence of the card itself.

varies.description: The checklist this one takes its card numbers from — normally "base.csv". Required on a variation, which by definition re-versions cards that already exist; optional elsewhere, because an autograph or relic of a base card shares its numbering too (2026 Topps Real One Relics are relics of base cards). Validation fails if any card number here is absent from that file, which is what stops a re-version being counted as an extra card. It is always asserted by a person and never inferred from numbers: 2026 Topps has a 90-card insert numbered 1-90 whose numbers all exist in the base set and whose players are entirely different.

card_count.description: Declared number of cards. Validation fails if the CSV row count differs.

distribution.description: Optional, as printed by the manufacturer: "Hobby Only", "Retail Exclusive"...

tags.description: Categories this checklist belongs to, from schema/1.0/tags.json; validation fails on a value not in that list. These are the repo's own categories rather than anything printed, so they are asserted by a person, and they exist to answer questions that span sets — every gimmick across every year — which `kind` cannot, since it says only that these are variations. A tag never restates data already held: distribution is `distribution`, short-printing is the row's `is_short_print`.

provenance.description: Every source the rows were derived from. An array, not one entry, because a set is usually published across several checklists — one per series, plus a factory-set checklist — and agreement between independent sources is the strongest verification this repo can offer.

source.description: What the data was derived from — a PDF's published title/filename, a page title. The source itself is NOT stored in this repo.

retrieved.description: When the data was derived from the source.

covers.description: Which part of the set this source documents, e.g. "Series 1 (#1-350)".

notes.description: Anything a reviewer needs: repairs applied, known gaps, disagreements with other sources.

series.description: The waves a set was issued in. Topps flagship is one 700-card set published as Series 1 and Series 2; they are not separate sets, and a factory set is a packaging of the whole.

card_numbers.description: The base range this wave carried, e.g. "1-350".

packagings.description: Ways the set was sold as a whole — a factory/complete set in a box, a team set. A packaging contains checklists that already exist above; it is never a separate set and never duplicates rows. This is what tells a collector exactly which cards a sealed factory set holds.

id.description: Permanent UUIDv4 for the packaging itself. A sealed factory set is a thing a collector owns and catalogues, so it gets the same stable handle a set does, unique across this repo.

type.description: What kind of packaging. A closed vocabulary, extended by amending this schema.

contains.description: The checklists in the box. Objects rather than plain filenames so a packaging holding only part of a checklist — a team set — can gain a card-number selector in a later revision without breaking this one.

file.description: A file from `checklists[].file`. Validation fails on a file this set does not declare.

exclusive.description: True when these cards are available only in this packaging. The 2026 Topps factory set holds the whole base set — the same cards found in packs — plus four short-print rookies sold no other way. Absent means false.

card_count.description: Physical cards in the packaging — the sum of the contained checklists' card_count, which validation enforces. A variation counts alongside the base card it varies, so this figure can exceed the set's distinct card numbers: the 2026 Topps factory set holds 704 cards drawn from 700 numbers.

distribution.description: Where it was sold, when a set has more than one factory set, e.g. "Hobby", "Retail".

parallels.description: Every parallel of this set lives here, and only here — one home, whether or not it has rows. A parallel uses the exact same photograph and design structure as a base card, but alters the color scheme, borders, card finish, or foil pattern; it never introduces a card, so it is never a checklist. A collection records "I own card #100 of this set as the Gold parallel" by pointing at a base row plus a parallel id. Whether a parallel carries rows is decided by one rule: rows exist only when they hold information that cannot be derived — the manufacturer printed an explicit partial list (`coverage: partial`, rows in `file`). A parallel covering every card of its target checklists is fully derivable and gets no rows (`coverage: full`); one whose extent nobody has verified is declared honestly as `coverage: unknown` rather than guessed.

then.description: A partial parallel's extent IS its rows: file, varies and card_count are required, and applies_to or series would duplicate what the rows already say.
A full-coverage parallel is derivable from its target checklists, so rows would be pure duplication; an unknown one has no rows to give. Neither may carry file, varies or card_count.

id.description: Permanent UUIDv4, unique across the repo. A parallel card is a thing a collector owns; ownership is recorded as (set, card_number, parallel id), so the id must survive renames.

coverage.description: What this parallel covers, asserted by a person, never inferred. full — every card of the target checklists (`applies_to`, or the whole set) exists in this parallel; validation may then treat the parent rows as this parallel's checklist. partial — only the cards listed in `file`, because the manufacturer printed an explicit list. unknown — the parallel exists but nobody has verified its extent; consumers must not assume any particular card exists in it. A checklist source that names a parallel without counting it supports exactly `unknown`, nothing stronger.

file.description: Rows of a partial parallel, in the 1.0 row format. Only coverage: partial has this — rows exist to carry the one fact that cannot be derived: WHICH cards got the treatment.

varies.description: The checklist a partial parallel's rows take their card numbers from — a file from `checklists[].file`. Validation fails on any card number absent from it, and fails a `file` whose numbers cover ALL of it: that parallel is coverage: full and needs no rows.

card_count.description: Declared number of rows in `file`. Validation fails if the CSV differs.

print_run.description: Serial-numbered run size, e.g. 2025 for /2025. Omit if unnumbered.

applies_to.description: What this parallel prints, named from `checklists[].name` or from another entry's `parallels[].name`; validation fails on a name this set declares in neither, on a parallel naming itself, and on a cycle. Omit = applies to the whole set. Only coverage: full and unknown use this — a partial parallel's extent is its rows. Naming a parallel is how a colour run of a parallel is recorded: 2025 Topps' Big Apple is a 100-card partial parallel of the base set, and its Gold, Orange, Black, Red and FoilFractor print those same 100 cards again. Without it the same programme is expressible only when its parent happens to be filed as a checklist. A set may not use one name for both a checklist and a parallel, which is what keeps this unambiguous.

series.description: The wave this parallel was printed in, naming an entry in `series[]`; validation fails on a name this set does not declare. It NARROWS the target before `coverage` is read: `coverage: full` with `series: "Series 1"` means every card of `applies_to` whose number falls in that series' range, not every card of the set. This is how a parallel covering one whole wave is recorded without rows — 2026 Topps' Spring Training prints all 350 Series 1 base cards and none of Series 2, which is neither full coverage of the 700 nor an arbitrary partial list, and the numbers stay derivable from `series[].card_numbers`. Omit when a parallel spans every wave.

verified.description: True only after a human has reviewed the rows against the source. Provenance is required regardless.
